text:
katie: Quick heads-up — planning a short maintenance/change window tonight to roll a model variant in EU (hosted + some Dedicated pools). Target start 2025-06-15 23:00 UTC, window ~45m. Need final customer-facing statuspage snippet + an email blurb ready. Any blockers?

dmitri: Sounds good from product. Two asks: 1) include a note about fallback pin for Dedicated customers, 2) include how we'll notify if rollback happens.

sam_ops: Ops ok, we'll pin v1.4.3 for Dedicated pools as a fallback and keep canary in hosted for 30m. Oncall will have rollback playbook ready. No infra changes.

katie: Perfect — lean status copy below, please review/edit: 

Statuspage snippet (short):
"We will perform a brief deployment to improve model latency and reliability in the EU region. Some customers on Dedicated capacity may be pinned to the previous model temporarily during the rollout. Updates will be posted here and via email. Expected impact: brief, targeted pinning for affected Dedicated pools. ETA 45 minutes."

lee_support: That reads customer-friendly. Suggest adding a link to the support KB for pins and what they see: /docs/dedicated/pinning (we'll paste full URL in final).

katie: Good call. Email blurb (one-paragraph):

"We are rolling an inference update in the EU region on 15 June at 23:00 UTC. Most customers will see no disruption. Customers on Dedicated capacity may be temporarily pinned to the previous model while we validate performance; this is expected to be brief. If you rely on strict model pinning or have a scheduled job overlapping the window, reply to this email and we'll coordinate. For more detail, see <https://status.redwood.ai> and our KB: https://docs.redwood.ai/dedicated/pinning."

dmitri: Nice. Can we add a single-line note for statuspage timeline?

katie: Added: "Start: 2025-06-15 23:00 UTC — Estimated complete: 2025-06-15 23:45 UTC. We will post updates every 10–15 minutes or on significant changes."

sam_ops: Ops checklist (short):
```
- Preflight: confirm canary passes smoke (latency, memory, p95 tokens)
- Deploy hosted canary -> monitor 10m
- If stable -> ramp to region; enable Dedicated pin fallback route
- If anomaly -> stop rollout, pin Dedicated to v1.4.3, trigger rollback and notify
- Post: run sanity queries and confirm metrics back to baseline
- Notify support + statuspage updates at major steps
```

sam_ops: Oncall is @dmitri for the window; backup @sam_ops. Pager is set.

deploybot: Automated note: Scheduled rollout job created: job_id=rb-20250615-9942, target=eu-west-1, model=redwood-llm-v1.5-quant. Canary window=10m. Fallback policy=pin-to-v1.4.3 for Dedicated if failure.

lee_support: Support copy for tickets (short):
"We are performing a planned model rollout in EU. If you notice changed behavior or increased latency, please reply here and include 'model-rollout-2025-06-15' in the subject. We will provide updates via status.redwood.ai."

dmitri: Rollback decision criteria (one-liners):
- p95 tokens increase > 40% vs baseline for 10m -> rollback
- error rate above 0.5% for 5m -> rollback
- degradation in correctness alerts from eval set -> pause and investigate

katie: Final ask: Lee, can you prep a 2-sentence SMS/short-email variant for customers opted into SMS? Keep it minimal; we only send if rollout extends beyond 60m or rollback occurs.

lee_support: SMS draft: "Redwood: We're deploying a model update in EU. Minor targeted impact possible for Dedicated customers. Updates: status.redwood.ai. Reply if urgent."

sam_ops: All set from ops. I'll push the canary at 23:00 UTC and post the first statuspage update when canary completes. If we need to pin/rollback I'll post here with 'ACTION: ROLLBACK' prefix.

katie: Thanks team — I'll queue the statuspage entries and the email blast. Posting final copy in #support for sign-off 30m before window. :spiral_calendar: :white_check_mark:
